svg.title: Drop - pin ladder
svg.text: One block per housing, one row per cavity. Every wire runs straight from its cavity to where it lands. Read left to right.
Laptop port in the glovebox — 120 Ω across 1/2 inside the plug
DP-ICU-A · DT06-6S · ICU unit rear wall, behind the display
ICU tail A — the DT06-6S plug from the post into the ICU's DT13-06PA (D-270)
ICU tail A (D-270) - the O20 bus, plain on/off with PARK / HEAD: it tells the display the lights are on;
the level comes in 0x300 byte 6 (D-462, D-567, D-577)
ICU tail A (D-270) — the display's backlight feed through the carrier (D-268)
DP-ICU-B · DT06-12S · ICU unit rear wall, behind the display
ICU tail B (D-270) — the ICU excites and reads the sender; the display draws it
ICU tail B (D-270) — a PMU-excited node the ICU reads (D-260); the display draws it
ICU tail B (D-270) — the ICU excites and reads the sender; the display draws it
ICU tail B (D-270) — read by the ICU
ICU tail B (D-270) — read by the ICU; the display draws the CHARGE tell-tale
ICU tail B (D-270) — read by the ICU; the display draws one BRAKE tell-tale for both switches

ICU tail B (D-270) — channel IC08; pulses per mile is a config value (D-272)
DP-ICU-B-9 · 16 AWG GRY · RT13 · capped at the far end
The ICU's spare input (DT13 pin 9) — nothing reads it until the swap brings a sensor; wired to L1-S2

Hatch release select - K3 coil return

along RT11. The DCU sinks it during the release pulse to pick the hatch (D-370) Was DP-DCU-B 10.

Servo +5 V rail - the three door servos
In the CMC 48 plug at the end of the L3 leg's Control Unit branch (D-582), in its HVAC breakout
down RT14. +5 V to all three door servos (DV59): one conductor to the HVAC case, split there to the
three JR leads (P172). The firmware moves one servo at a time (F-017), so the conductor carries one
servo's stall current, 1-2.5 A. The far end stays capped until the luxury package fits the load Was

while it stays) joined in one splice behind the centre stack; Their current returns through the
